canonical_statement: The study aimed to estimate the effectiveness of nirsevimab in reducing antibiotic prescribing for acute respiratory tract infections in outpatient and inpatient settings among infants in their first RSV season during 2023-2025.

canonical_statement: The retrospective observational cohort used electronic health record data from 32 pediatric primary care practices to emulate a target trial of nirsevimab versus no nirsevimab.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: observational study cohort to emulate a sequence of target trials

canonical_statement: The 2023-2024 RSV season was defined as 16 October 2023 through 31 March 2024 and the 2024-2025 season as 3 October 2024 through 31 March 2025; the seasons were combined for analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The 2023–2024 RSV season was defined as 16 October 2023 through 31 March 2024

canonical_statement: The target trial protocol was developed according to the TARGET reporting guideline, and the observational study emulated a sequence of target trials.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The target trial protocol was developed according to the Transparent Reporting of Observational Studies Emulating a Target Trial (TARGET) guideline

canonical_statement: The study period was divided into six monthly sequential trial intervals; infants who remained eligible could contribute to multiple sequential trials until an outcome occurred.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: implemented a sequential trial design by dividing the study period into 6 monthly intervals

canonical_statement: At each emulated trial baseline, treatment strategy was assigned according to nirsevimab administration recorded in the medication administration record; infants without nirsevimab at time zero were assigned to the nontreatment strategy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Infants were assigned to the treatment strategy corresponding to whether nirsevimab was administered at time zero

canonical_statement: Within each emulated trial, infants were followed for up to six months or until the outcome; infants without recorded outcomes were assumed to remain under observation until administrative end of follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Within each trial, patients were followed up to 6 months or censored at the time of the outcome

canonical_statement: Discretizing nirsevimab receipt and outcome dates into monthly intervals created an implicit one-month grace period; temporally inconsistent eligible trial records were randomly assigned to one of the two treatment strategies, and the target estimand was the intention-to-treat effect.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The target estimand was the intention-to-treat effect

canonical_statement: Cumulative risks were estimated with marginal structural models using pooled logistic regression for discrete-time hazards, with adjustment for age at trial start, sex, race, medical complexity, practice membership, and RSV season period; robust sandwich variance estimators accounted for repeated observations within infants.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used marginal structural models to estimate cumulative risks under each treatment strategy

canonical_statement: Nirsevimab effectiveness at six months was defined as 1 minus the risk ratio derived from estimated cumulative risks, with 95% confidence intervals approximated using the Delta method.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Nirsevimab effectiveness (NE) at 6 months was calculated as NE = 1 − RR

canonical_statement: Data were extracted on 25 July 2025; all data fields were manually validated in 100 randomly selected EHR charts, and analyses used R version 4.3.2 with the TrialEmulation package.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All data fields were validated via manual review of 100 randomly selected charts in the EHR

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that nirsevimab administration reduced antibiotic use for acute respiratory tract infections across outpatient and inpatient settings.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Nirsevimab administration reduced antibiotic use for ARTIs across settings

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that the reduction in antibiotic use appeared to be driven largely by reduced prescribing for viral infections and acute otitis media and argued that increasing nirsevimab coverage could supplement antibiotic stewardship efforts.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This decrease in antibiotic use appears to be driven largely by a reduction in antibiotic prescribing for both viral infections and AOM

canonical_statement: The authors noted that studying a single pediatric care network across Pennsylvania and New Jersey may limit national generalizability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Because this study exclusively evaluated a pediatric care network across Pennsylvania and New Jersey, our findings may not be nationally generalizable

canonical_statement: The retrospective EHR design was subject to possible exposure and outcome misclassification, including antibiotic use occurring at outside hospitals or urgent care centers that was not recorded in the network EHR.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: this study was limited by data recorded in the EHR and, therefore, is subject to potential misclassification of exposures

canonical_statement: The study could not account for potential unmeasured confounders such as healthcare utilization that could be related to both nirsevimab receipt and medically attended encounters.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We also could not account for potential unmeasured confounders, such as healthcare utilization
